Just to place this in context: the civil service exam is arguably one of, if not *the* toughest exams in the world. It covers an astonishing amount of material. The exam has two rounds. The first round has objective, multiple choice questions covering mathematics, general reasoning and general knowledge about history, culture, science and arts. If you clear the first round (a small fraction of applicants), you go to round II. Round II is *extremely* comprehensive. It has 7 subjective, essay-like papers covering everything from government policy to language, history, art, culture and science. The questions are obscure and demand a thorough knowledge and understanding of the subject. I know some really smart people who've studied two years straight and fail to crack this exam. And by two years straight, I mean *literally* leaving work and staying at home for two whole years just to study. With the assistance of a tutor. I consider myself smart enough, but if I was asked to appear for this exam, I'd run as fast as I could in the opposite direction.

You get to join the elite civil services. This is an elite cadre of bureaucrats - a holdover from the colonial era. Basically, these are people who run the country. The executive branch, if you will. The top rank holders get to join the top administrative service. Each officer is like a Mayor. The next rank holders get to join the police service. All of the country's top police officers - police commissioners, state police chiefs, etc. Ambassadors and diplomats are chosen from this exam as well. Basically, these people have a lot of power and thus, respect in society. Imagine the kind of respect your mayor or local police chief gets, then multiply that by 10x since these are government bureaucrats and thus, hold office pretty much until retirement.

Hindi is a crappy language. I seriously love words and languages. But Hindi is just ugly now. It's completely bastardized to the point that it has hardly any of its own words any more. So many Hindi words are basically dead. "Doorbhash", "Prasar", "Sanchalan". You'll never find these words outside of official communication. Everyday Hindi has no beauty to it at all. It's merely a functional language. Try doing it: when you're talking to someone in Hindi, note the words you use. You'll realize that you use Hindi words mostly to communicate functional things ("where", "when", "how") and use loan words from English for anything conceptual. Hindi needs serious reform before it can aspire to be India's national language

T20 misses one of the most important elements of the game: strategy. The sport is as much a game of leadership and strategy as it is a game of skill and athleticism. The longer format of the sport captures it perfectly. Teams are defined by their captains (i.e. their leaders) and the decisions they make. This is something missing from nearly every other sport. Does a soccer team captain change his lineup based on the condition of the ground? Does the thought it might rain 3 days later change a baseball team's selection?  It's all these things, plus the sheer elegance of the game that make it so amazing to me. I mean, look at a top batsman playing different shots. The physical gestures of all these shots - especially the drives and pulls - feels almost like a dance.  The sport is such an amazing game and the only format of it that captures the true spirit is test matches. I like my T20s because they're lots of fun, but test cricket is art, man.
